gap: None of the results ChatGPT got says that Plex's own hardware-transcoding page (last modified 2026-10-27) lists only Intel (Quick Sync/VAAPI) and NVIDIA engines on Linux and mentions only Intel Quick Sync for Docker; AMD appears only in the Windows notes, supported 'as is' and not fully tested. On the stated record, the AMD all-in-ones ChatGPT offered, such as the Aoostar WTR Pro 5825U as 'best for internal HDD storage', have no documented Plex hardware transcoding under Proxmox, Unraid or TrueNAS.
standout_why: Rival pages compared: littlecompute.com/best-mini-pc-for-plex says AMD's 780M 'handles Plex fine' and 'works too'. bitdoze.com/best-mini-pc-proxmox says AMD VAAPI 'can work' but reports no Plex result. homelabcompass.com (cited) recommends Quick Sync but never says whether AMD works. Our own page only says 'AMD graphics, no Quick Sync', and its table also lacks a common configured-price column. ChatGPT's answers say only that AMD is 'less straightforward'. None of these cites Plex's own Linux and Docker engine list. None puts barebone and configured prices on one basis either: ChatGPT showed the MS-01 SE at '$369 barebone' and budgeted '$100 for 32GB DDR5'. Against that, Minisforum's own store has the SE barebone at $375, and StarryHope lists $775 for 32GB/1TB, so RAM plus SSD adds $400.
decides: Two corrections decide the pick. (1) Plex transcoding: for the branch where media drives go inside the box, the AMD boxes fall out (WTR Pro 5825U, WTR Max 8845HS, GMKtec K8 Plus) because Plex documents no hardware transcoding for them on Linux. That leaves Intel bay boxes: the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at $619.99 with 8 GB included, or the Aoostar WTR Max Intel i5-1235U at $529 barebone with 6 HDD bays, 2× 10GbE and DDR5 up to 96 GB, before RAM. (2) Price on one basis: price every option as configured with 32 GB RAM and 1 TB NVMe, no hard drives. On that basis the 'cheap' $375 MS-01 SE barebone becomes $775 and the MS-01's DDR5 is costlier still: bitdoze priced a 32 GB DDR5 kit at $569.98. So a mini PC with RAM included, or a NAS that ships with RAM, beats a barebone plus retail DDR5 under $800. The table footnote should be: 'Plex HW transcode on Linux/Docker = Intel or NVIDIA only (Plex support, 2026-10-27); barebone prices shown as configured at 32 GB / 1 TB.'

findings.label: Plex hardware transcoding engines on Linux and in Docker
findings.value: Linux: Intel VAAPI and NVIDIA (NVDEC/NVENC) only. Docker: only Intel Quick Sync is mentioned, and it needs Plex Pass. AMD appears only in the Windows notes, as 'as is' with no full testing.
findings.note: Page says 'Last modified on: October 27, 2026'. VAAPI is listed only as an Intel engine, and the page says nothing about AMD on Linux. It recommends 'Intel Quick Sync Video or a dedicated NVIDIA GPU'.
